principle: PRECEPTA patterns are human-readable, stigma-free descriptions that emerge from combinations of DYNAMOS dimensions. No single dimension defines a pattern.

patterns.name: Deep Systems Architect
patterns.description: Naturally perceives problems as systems rather than isolated elements. Excels at identifying structural gaps, dependencies, and long-term implications, especially in complex or abstract domains.

patterns.name: Precision Resolver
patterns.description: Experiences strong internal pressure to eliminate errors, inconsistencies, or unfinished structures. Thrives when problems can be refined to clarity and completion, but may find ambiguity or partial solutions costly.

patterns.name: Fast Insight / Slow Explanation
patterns.description: Arrives at understanding rapidly and often non-linearly, but needs additional time or effort to translate insights into step-by-step explanations. Others may underestimate the depth of reasoning because intermediate steps are skipped internally.

patterns.name: Divergent Idea Generator
patterns.description: Generates novel ideas and unconventional approaches with ease, especially when exploration is encouraged. May prioritize creativity over completion and benefit from external structures that support follow-through.

patterns.name: Domain-Locked Expert
patterns.description: Develops exceptional depth and expertise within specific interest areas. Performs best when work aligns closely with established domains of meaning and may disengage sharply outside those contexts.

patterns.name: Split-Integration Thinker
patterns.description: Shows strong conceptual reasoning while having limited access to emotional labeling or articulation. Emotions are present and influential but are processed indirectly rather than through explicit awareness.

patterns.name: Big-Picture Synthesizer
patterns.description: Naturally integrates information across time, domains, and perspectives. Prefers abstraction and synthesis over detail work and often contributes strategic or visionary insight.

patterns.name: Executive-Load Taxed
patterns.description: Handles complexity well in principle but experiences high cost when multiple executive demands stack. Task switching, coordination, or administrative overhead can disproportionately reduce effectiveness.

patterns.name: Flow Diver
patterns.description: Enters deep focus states readily when conditions are right and remains absorbed for extended periods. Disengaging or switching tasks can be difficult and costly once immersion has occurred.

patterns.name: Meaning-Gated Performer
patterns.description: Engagement and performance depend strongly on perceived meaning or relevance. When alignment is present, output is high; when absent, activation becomes effortful or unsustainable.

patterns.name: Burst Creator
patterns.description: Works in intense, high-energy bursts followed by periods of low output or disengagement. Performs best with flexible pacing and may struggle in environments requiring steady, uniform productivity.

patterns.name: Routine Anchor
patterns.description: Relies on predictability and established routines to maintain stability and performance. Unexpected changes or disruptions may cause stress, even if overall capability remains high.

patterns.name: Deadline-Unlocked Starter
patterns.description: Activation increases sharply as external time pressure approaches. Can perform very effectively under deadlines but may experience unnecessary stress or volatility as a result.

patterns.name: Long-Horizon Planner
patterns.description: Thinks naturally in extended timeframes and maintains continuity across long projects. Prefers strategic planning and future-oriented work over short-term task cycling.

patterns.name: Transition-Fragile
patterns.description: Experiences significant cost when moving between tasks, states, or contexts. May perform well once settled but find beginnings and endings disproportionately demanding.

patterns.name: Start–Stop Oscillator
patterns.description: Cycles between engagement and disengagement due to regulation or recovery limits. Patterns may appear inconsistent externally despite strong capability during active phases.

patterns.name: Precision Literalist
patterns.description: Communicates directly, accurately, and with minimal reliance on subtext. Values clarity and correctness over social smoothing, which can sometimes be misinterpreted by others.

patterns.name: Social Cue Load
patterns.description: Finds real-time social interpretation cognitively demanding. Social difficulties arise from processing load rather than lack of interest or concern for others.

patterns.name: Low-Feedback Autonomy
patterns.description: Self-regulates primarily through internal standards rather than external validation. Functions well independently and is relatively unaffected by praise or criticism.

patterns.name: Impulsive / Enthusiastic Communicator
patterns.description: Expresses thoughts and excitement quickly and openly, sometimes before full filtering. Communication energy can be engaging but may occasionally overwhelm conversational pacing.

patterns.name: Masked High-Cost Performer
patterns.description: Maintains socially expected behavior through conscious regulation rather than ease. Performance appears smooth externally but carries significant internal cost over time.

patterns.name: Ethical Precision Speaker
patterns.description: Is guided by strong internal values around fairness, truth, and responsibility in communication. May correct inaccuracies or challenge inconsistencies even in informal contexts.

patterns.name: Affective Floodgate
patterns.description: Experiences emotions intensely and with limited buffering once thresholds are crossed. Emotional overwhelm can emerge suddenly under cumulative load.

patterns.name: Social Rejection Amplifier
patterns.description: Reacts strongly to perceived criticism or rejection, even when subtle or unintended. Sensitivity reflects heightened feedback gain rather than fragility or insecurity.

patterns.name: Ethical Amplifier
patterns.description: Responds deeply to issues of justice, fairness, and moral coherence. Ethical violations or value conflicts are difficult to ignore and may drive sustained engagement or distress.

patterns.name: Verification Loop
patterns.description: Feels compelled to re-check, refine, or perfect work to ensure correctness. This can enhance quality but may also prolong tasks or increase cognitive load.

patterns.name: Affective Decoupler
patterns.description: Processes emotions internally without readily identifying or verbalizing them. Emotional awareness may emerge indirectly through behavior, values, or delayed reflection.

patterns.name: Open-Plan Vulnerable
patterns.description: Is sensitive to sensory-rich environments such as noise, movement, or visual clutter. Performance improves significantly in controlled or quieter settings.

patterns.name: Sensory-Seeking Stabilizer
patterns.description: Uses movement, stimulation, or sensory input to regulate attention and energy. Physical engagement supports cognitive focus rather than distracting from it.

patterns.name: Quiet-Need Deep Worker
patterns.description: Performs best in low-stimulation environments that protect focus and continuity. Sensory calm enables sustained deep work and high-quality output.

patterns.name: Stim-Regulation Loop
patterns.description: Engages in repetitive movements or sensory actions to self-regulate. These behaviors support stability and concentration and are adaptive rather than problematic.

patterns.name: Time-Blind Sprinter
patterns.description: Experiences time subjectively rather than linearly. May underestimate duration or urgency but can perform effectively once engaged or externally anchored.
